[Pedagogy audit v2 · New question to decide] For the type count gap (line-equation-from-inclination-diagram). Comparison score 48, between p62-q7-block and p63-q10-block: The inclination has to be read from a diagram. In part b the marked 30° is not the inclination, so the student must see that it is 150°. Then comes exact tan, a point or intercept from the diagram, and exact general form with surds. That is more interpretation than p62-q7 but less than the multi-part coordinate geometry of p63-q10.
Proposed question: Determine the equation of each straight line sketched below in exact general form.
a) (with a diagram)
b) (with a diagram)
Answers: a) $\sqrt3x-y-3\sqrt3=0$. Use $m=\tan60^{\circ}=\sqrt3$ and the point $(3,0)$.; b) $x+\sqrt3y-6\sqrt3=0$. The inclination is $180^{\circ}-30^{\circ}=150^{\circ}$, so $m=-\dfrac1{\sqrt3}$; the $y$-intercept is $6$.
